headline: The worst is behind us: Wednesday's burst pushed the channel at Caltrain to 4.4 ft (above Watch) and the early-morning band to 2.53 ft; what's left is showers, with the consensus for the wettest 3 hours down to about 0.39 in, well below Yellow.

summary.text: Consensus for the wettest 3 hours fell from 0.99 in to 0.39 in as the front moved through. Only scattered showers are left, with a Friday-morning round the wettest.
Wettest 3 hours in the next 72 h: RRFS 0.39 in, HRRR 0.34, GFS 0.34, NBM 0.25, ECMWF 0.10. Consensus (HRRR ×1.25 = 0.42, RRFS 0.39, NBM 0.25: middle value) 0.39 in.
At most water on the sidewalk in a heavy shower. Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours, nearly double the wettest model, or a measured 0.40 in hour.
Showers on and off today. HRRR has one strong cell near 10 PM tonight (0.34 in) that no other model shows. RRFS and NBM favor a wetter stretch about 4 to 9 AM Friday.
Friday's 7.9 ft high tide at 8:32 AM runs about 9.9 ft on the NOAA Bay model (~2 ft surge), right on top of Friday's shower round. Caltrain channel is back down to 0.34 ft.
No cars need to move for now. Clear leaves off drain grates today, and check the page around 10 PM tonight and 6–9 AM Friday.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: The main storm is past. Wednesday's front brought a record day to downtown San Francisco (2.64 in, per NWS), and an intense rain band crossed the Bay Area again early this morning. The upper low is now sliding south through the region. NWS San Francisco expects numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms with small hail through today and into Friday morning, with some cells possibly moving over the same areas repeatedly. A colder front late tonight into Friday gradually cuts the showers back. A weaker system Saturday afternoon favors the North Bay, and NWS flags Tuesday into Wednesday of next week as the next chance for heavier rain (mainly North Bay) plus more coastal flooding from high tides.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
Since Wednesday morning's discussion the heavy rain has come and gone. Wednesday's peak at the Caltrain rain gauge was 0.52 in in the 11 AM hour and about 0.88 in from 11 AM to 2 PM, close to the 0.99 in consensus at the time, and the dashboard's storm library now lists Nov 18 as a garage-level storm. The early-morning band today added 0.28 in from 3 to 6 AM.

Looking ahead, the numbers are much smaller. Wettest 3 hours in the next 72 hours: RRFS (10 PM Wed run) 0.39 in, centered around 5 to 7 AM Friday with a 0.27 in hour; HRRR (8 AM run) 0.34 in, almost all in one hour near 10 PM tonight; GFS 0.34 in (it copies HRRR early on); NBM 0.25 in, spread over 7 to 9 AM Friday; ECMWF 0.10 in, this morning. The HRRR's 10 PM hour stands alone: no other model has more than 0.03 in then, so I treat it as a possible shower or thunderstorm cell, not a trend. The 15-minute HRRR puts 0.09 in in the quarter-hour at 10 PM.

The dashboard's consensus (HRRR ×1.25 = 0.42, RRFS 0.39, NBM 0.25; middle value) is 0.39 in, down from 0.99 in. That seems about right for a showery pattern, but a thunderstorm can easily beat any of these models over a small area; that is the main way this ends up worse.

Storm totals for the next 72 hours are light: RRFS 0.65 in, GFS 0.64, NBM 0.62, HRRR 0.49 (its run ends about 48 hours out), ECMWF 0.42.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
The Bay is running about 1.5 to 2.2 ft above the predicted tide on NOAA's Bay model. This morning's 7.4 ft high (7:58 AM) reached about 9.6 ft on the model. The tide is falling toward a 2.1 ft low at 2:22 PM (model about 3.7 ft). Tonight's 6.2 ft high at 8:09 PM shows about 8.3 ft on the model, so drainage is slower around the HRRR's 10 PM cell. Friday's 7.9 ft high at 8:32 AM shows about 9.9 ft, the highest of the next two days, and it lines up with the RRFS and NBM Friday-morning showers. NWS has a Coastal Flood Advisory for the Bay shoreline until 1 AM tonight and again 4 to 10 AM Friday.

Channel: the gauge upstream of Caltrain peaked at 4.4 ft at 11:49 AM Wednesday, above county Flood Watch (4.1 ft). This morning's band brought it back up to 2.53 ft from 4:51 to 5:10 AM, just short of Flood Monitoring (2.8 ft). It has drained down to 0.34 ft as of 10 AM. At Alameda de las Pulgas the channel peaked at 1.68 ft at 4:40 AM and is at 0.29 ft now (Monitoring 3.18 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Quiet at the moment. The Caltrain rain gauge has 1.44 in in the last 24 hours, but its last reading came in at 5:58 AM, with nothing in the 3 hours before that; the rain sensor reports when rain falls, so no new reading suggests little or no rain there since. Both channel gauges are low and falling. Note: a Tsunami Warning message from 9:30 to 10:30 AM was labeled TEST by the National Tsunami Warning Center; it was not a real warning.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Low for widespread rain, moderate for a single cell. The models agree that no long soaking rain is left, but they disagree on where the stronger showers go: HRRR puts its best cell tonight, while RRFS and NBM prefer Friday morning. In this kind of pattern an isolated thunderstorm can drop a lot in 20 to 30 minutes over a few blocks, and none of the models can place that ahead of time. Ground and the channel are already wet, so a burst would run off fast, and Friday's high tide with surge would slow drainage. Most likely outcome: no street flooding, possibly some water on the sidewalk in a downpour. The dashboard's measured-burst rule (0.40 in in one hour means at least Yellow) is the alarm to watch.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• No need to move cars for now; revisit if the 1-hour burst alarm trips or a thunderstorm warning comes in.
• During a dry break today, clear leaves and debris left by Wednesday's winds from the street drain grates and yard drains.
• Check the dashboard around 10 PM tonight and 6 to 9 AM Friday, when the models and the high tide line up.
• If there were photos of the street at Wednesday's peak, keep them with their times; they help calibrate the thresholds.
• Expect cold mornings Friday and Saturday.
• Don't drive or walk through moving water.
